bug_semantics: OpenMcdf name lookup in DirectoryTree.TryGetDirectoryEntry walks CFB directory sibling links in a while (child is not null) BST loop with no cycle detection. A crafted compound file whose Left/Right sibling pointers form a cycle that still satisfies per-step BST-order checks never reaches a null child or a matching name, so OpenStorage/TryOpenStorage/OpenStream/TryOpenStream hang uninterruptably. Enumeration later gained Brent cycle detection, but the lookup path did not.
flaw_origin: Original DirectoryTree feature. Commit 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344 first added OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTree.cs with TryGetDirectoryEntry walking LeftSiblingId/RightSiblingId until null or a name match and no visited-set or cycle bound. The parent tree has no DirectoryTree.cs; parent name lookup in DirectoryTreeEnumerator.TryGetDirectoryEntry iterated MoveNext() over a stack walk rather than this unbounded BST descent. Later rename OpenMcdf3 to OpenMcdf, TryGetSibling/validateColor, and enumerator-only Brent detection carried the same lookup loop until c6f82db722bd85db7b0caed3ca1aa374f1e07bc7.

reasoning: The hang is a real CWE-835 on an untrusted CFB directory tree: name lookup follows sibling IDs until null without a cycle bound, so a cyclic BST-order-satisfying graph never exits. That loop is first written in 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344 when DirectoryTree.cs is added; the parent has no such file and used enumerator scan for name lookup. Rename, TryGetSibling/validateColor, and enumerator-only Brent detection are not first-writes of the lookup hang. Direct closure is c6f82db722bd85db7b0caed3ca1aa374f1e07bc7, which injects a search-order validator into the lookup walk. The BIC commit object is human-authored/committed with no AI marker, so the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI.
